newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Peugeot Nigeria hopes elections will boost sales.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot Nigeria hopes elections will boost sales.

text.p: Peugeot Automobile Nigeria hopes the military government's plan to hold elections and restore civilian rule will increase car sales and allow it to double production at its assembly plant.
"The politicians will need our cars to get to the hard to reach rural areas and we will target them for sales," Peugeot spokesman Balarabe Muhammad told Reuters at a Lagos motor show at the weekend.
"We hope to be assembling 60 cars a day before the end of the year from 30 cars a day now."
Nigeria's military leader General Sani Abacha last year set out a timetable to restore civilian rule by October 1998.
The electoral commission is soon expected to announce which of 15 aspiring political parties will be allowed to take part in the elections.
Multiparty local elections are scheduled before the end of the year.
At one time Africa's most populous nation had six vehicle assembly plants. Now it has only the Peugeot.
Production at the plant in the northern city of Kaduna has risen to around 30 vehicles per day in 1996 from 15 to 20 in 1995.
But this is far from 150 per day in 1991 and 260 per day in the early 1980s, when Nigeria rode high on booming crude oil revenues.
Muhammad said Peugeot cars assembled in Nigeria account for up to 80 percent of cars used by government, which has adopted them as official vehicles.
Economic decline has shadowed Nigeria's political crisis which erupted in 1993, when a previous military government annulled elections that would have ended a decade of army rule.
